messages:
maya: Quick post-design-review note — the revoke key modal feels heavy. Two things I noticed: the full explanation text + the destructive CTA compete visually, and screen-reader focus lands on the CTA instead of the confirmation copy.

kai: Agreed. The modal currently shows the long justification text first, then the CTA row. Feels like we’re surfacing the worst bit up front.

olivia: +1. Could we try progressive disclosure? Show a short one-line summary and a “Why this matters” expander that reveals the longer explanation.

maya: That was my thought. Short primary line: “This action will immediately revoke access for any apps using this key.” Then a small link: “Why revoke?” -> expands full paragraph and list of who is impacted.

raghu: For accessibility we should ensure the expander uses aria-expanded and focus stays sensible. Right now the keyboard tab order jumps from the close button to the destructive button — screen readers miss the context.

design-bot: Suggestion: move the confirmation sentence to directly precede the primary CTA so that SR users hear the risk before the button. Also add aria-live="polite" to the modal announcement so users know when the key is revoked.

maya: UX copy tweak proposal: primary summary + small gray helper text under it with the short reason. CTA copy: “Revoke key” (primary, destructive). Secondary: “Cancel”. Add an inline “Undo” toast suggestion copy that appears for 15s after revoke. Thoughts?

kai: Love the undo toast. But want product clarity on scope: undo should only re-enable the specific key metadata (not any downstream tokens). Can confirm with backend team?

olivia: I'll check with infra. If undo is supported we should design the toast affordance to be keyboard accessible (focusable) and include aria-label like "Undo revoke for <key-name>".

raghu: Accessibility nit: when the modal opens set focus to the modal container h1, not the first button. Announce the short summary via aria-labelledby. Then users can tab to the expander or CTA.

maya: UX microcopy draft for expanded content (for review):
"Revoking this API key immediately prevents any application using it from authenticating. If you're unsure which services depend on this key, expand 'Why revoke?' for a list of recent callers and recommended mitigation steps"

olivia: Nice. Minor wording: change "recent callers" to "recent callers and active routes" to surface which routes will fail.

maya: Updated: "...expand 'Why revoke?' for a list of recent callers and active routes, plus recommended mitigation steps."

kai: Design request: can we reduce modal height by collapsing the list of callers by default (show up to 3 rows and a "show more")? Long lists feel overwhelming.

maya: Yes. Collapsed list + link to usage page for full history. Also keep a small inline risk indicator (color + screen-reader text) next to the key name: e.g., "High impact — used by 4 live routes".

raghu: For color contrast: avoid relying on color alone. Add an icon and sr-only text for the impact level. Also ensure contrast ratio meets AA on the helper chips.

design-bot: Quick CSS/spec note: destructive CTA should have focus ring 3px #FFB4B4 on hover/focus to meet contrast; undo toast should be reachable with Shift+Tab from the main content flow.

olivia: I'll mock this in Figma and attach a link. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XXXXX/revoke-modal-proposal (WIP)

maya: Thanks — next steps: olivia to push updated mock + copy by EOD, raghu to verify focus behavior, kai to confirm backend undo feasibility. I'll synthesize into a small PR for copy changes once we have the Figma.

kai: SG. If backend can't support undo, we still keep the expander + progressive disclosure — UX win on its own.

olivia: Will post prototype + a11y checklist here when ready.

maya: Tiny remaining question: do we keep a separate danger banner on the credentials list page when a revoke has happened? I think yes — a contextual banner linking to an incident timeline.

raghu: Banner is fine. Make sure it uses role="status" and isn't announced repeatedly when the page reloads.

maya: Great. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

(End thread)
